Understanding the approach

Conflict sits within a larger relationship.

The Gottman Method organizes work around a relationship framework that includes friendship, responding to bids for connection, managing conflict, and creating shared meaning. Trust and commitment are important parts of that framework. The emphasis is not only on what happens during an argument but also on the everyday relationship around it.

Gottman-informed therapy may draw on selected ideas or interventions from this approach. That description is different from confirming a particular certification level, a complete assessment package, or use of every part of the method. The actual plan should reflect the clinician's training and the couple's needs.

One useful distinction is between addressing a specific complaint and attacking a person's character. Another is between interrupting escalation and resolving the underlying disagreement. A calmer conversation can create room for the issue; it does not automatically settle it.

Sources gottman gottman-conflict

In plain language

Learn about each other, not a set of scores.

A framework can organize questions. It cannot decide whether your relationship is healthy, whether both people are safe, or what the future should be from a few online examples.

A worked example

The dishes are the topic. Feeling alone is part of the experience.

This fictional example concerns an ordinary household disagreement between partners who can speak safely.

Fictional teaching example. Not a diagnosis, a client story, or an assigned exercise.

01

The opening

Alex comes home to a kitchen full of dishes and says, You never help. Riley hears an accusation about their character and starts listing everything they did that day.

02

The escalation

The discussion moves away from the kitchen into a contest about who contributes more. Both people become focused on defending themselves instead of agreeing on what needs doing.

03

A possible repair

Alex notices the conversation is getting sharper and asks to restart with one specific concern. Riley is free to say they need a pause before returning to the issue.

What changes when the request becomes specific?

A restart could identify the concrete observation, describe its impact, and make a manageable request. It could also include recognition that work done elsewhere is real. This does not guarantee agreement about fairness, but it makes the subject easier to discuss than a global judgment about a partner.

The repair is only one piece. A lasting change might require an actual division-of-labor conversation and follow-through. Repeating apologies or softer wording without changing responsibilities would leave the substantive issue unresolved.

Sources gottman gottman-conflict

Go a little deeper

Four areas that can make the method easier to understand.

These are educational descriptions, not a complete Gottman assessment or an assigned couple exercise.

01Friendship and knowing each otherKeep an interest in the person whose life is changing alongside yours.Read more +

Knowing a partner is not a one-time task completed early in a relationship. Interests, stressors, hopes, and responsibilities can change. Gottman-informed work may include attention to that ongoing knowledge rather than concentrating exclusively on problems.

Curiosity is different from surveillance. Privacy and personal boundaries still matter.

02Bids and everyday responsesNotice the small invitations that can be easy to miss.Read more +

A bid for connection may be a question, a comment, an expression of interest, or a request for attention. The idea is to consider how ordinary responses contribute to connection, not to tally every missed cue as evidence of rejection.

A response can include a respectful limit and a later opportunity to connect.

03Conflict and repairReduce destructive exchanges while keeping the actual issue in view.Read more +

The approach describes patterns such as criticism, contempt, defensiveness, and withdrawal during overwhelming interactions. The value of the terms is noticing a behavior that could change, not labeling a partner as the problem.

Repair attempts and pauses should support returning to a conversation safely. They do not require immediate forgiveness.

04Meaning, dreams and differencesUnderstand what an issue represents before trying to solve it.Read more +

A disagreement can connect to personal values, family experiences, or hopes for the future. Some differences need ongoing management rather than a final winner. Learning what matters to each person can change the quality of the discussion.

Understanding why something matters is not the same as agreeing to it.

Sources gottman gottman-conflict

Inside the work

Assessment, practice, and application belong together.

01

Understand the relationship

A clinician may ask about history, strengths, stressors, conflict, and individual perspectives. Confirm which assessment and individual-contact policies actually apply.

02

Choose the work

The plan might focus on friendship, a recurring conflict, rebuilding trust, or discussing shared meaning. A method should not require ignoring the concern that brought you in.

03

Try and reflect

Practice may happen during the session with therapist feedback. What is useful for one couple may need adaptation for another.

04

Review the daily difference

Look beyond whether an exercise went smoothly. Consider whether the couple communicates more clearly, follows through, and experiences meaningful change outside appointments.

Sources gottman gottman-conflict

Fit, choice and limitations

Research-informed does not mean one exercise fits everyone.

No relationship verdict from a label

A webpage cannot predict divorce or score a relationship from a few examples. Named patterns are a language for exploring behavior, not an automated diagnosis or proof that a relationship is beyond repair.

The clinician and service still matter

Gottman-informed describes an influence on the work. Ask about relevant training, the process offered, and how concerns about fit are handled. Do not infer certification from a method name on a profile.

Sources gottman gottman-conflict

An important boundary

Safety comes before joint work.

Communication tools are not a treatment for coercion or a requirement to remain in an unsafe relationship. A clinician must assess safety and appropriateness before joint exercises, and harmful behavior remains the responsibility of the person doing it.

Sources relationship-safety

Private support comes first

Discuss safety and the appropriateness of shared sessions privately with a clinician.

Your questions, answered

More to know before choosing.

Will every disagreement be solved?

No method can promise that. Some disagreements concern lasting differences. A useful aim may be understanding and managing those differences without repeated injury, while identifying where actual decisions and commitments are needed.

Do both partners have homework?

Some clinicians suggest between-session practice. Ask what it involves and how it will be adapted to your circumstances. An activity should not become a tool to pressure or police the other person.

Is a repair the same as an apology?

Not always. A repair can be an attempt to interrupt escalation or restart a conversation. An apology can acknowledge responsibility. Neither replaces the behavior change or accountability that a particular hurt may require.

How is this different from EFT?

Gottman-informed work organizes attention around friendship, conflict, meaning, trust, and commitment. Emotionally Focused Therapy emphasizes attachment and emotional interactions. Clinicians may integrate ideas, but a coherent plan is more important than combining labels.

Are the listed clinicians certified Gottman therapists?

This page does not make that claim. It links only to profiles naming Gottman-informed work or the approach. Certification and current availability require separate confirmation.

What about private pay?

Couples consultations and couples sessions at M.F.T. are private pay. Request the fee and intended appointment type before booking; an approach name does not determine insurance coverage.

For practical questions, contact the support team. Please keep clinical details out of the initial email.
